content: A publication-quality event study paper contains: (1) Event definition section — precise event date (tau=0), selection criteria, confounding-event screening. (2) Data and Methods — estimation window [T0,T1], event window [T1+1,T2], return model specification (market model, FF3/FF5, Carhart), reference index, return type. (3) Results — AR/CAR tables for single-event; AAR/CAAR tables with test statistics (Patell Z, BMP, Sign, KP, t-test) for multi-event; significance stars. (4) Robustness checks — window sensitivity, model sensitivity, equal- vs value-weighted returns, bootstrap alongside asymptotic tests, subsample validation. (5) Cross-sectional regression (optional) — CARs regressed on firm characteristics. (6) Discussion/caveats — joint hypothesis problem (model + event), confounding events, calendar clustering, limitations. (7) References. Standard methodological references: MacKinlay (1997), Campbell/Lo/MacKinlay (1997), Kothari/Warner (2007).
